references.title: Fred Dretske, “Epistemic Operators” (1970), The Journal of Philosophy 67(24): 1007–1023
references.support: Original article bibliographic record. The JSTOR reproduction exposed metadata only during this review; the zebra passage (pp. 1015–1016) was checked through the quoted and analyzed passage in the Stanford Encyclopedia entry on epistemic closure.

references.title: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy: Epistemic Closure
references.support: Sections 1, 2.1–2.2, and 5.1–5.2 discuss qualified closure principles, quote and analyze Dretske's zebra/mule example (1970, pp. 1015–1016), explain relevant-alternatives and tracking responses, and present the closure-based skeptical inference and a Moorean reply. Secondary reference work; its analysis does not settle the debate.

references.title: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy: Epistemic Contextualism
references.support: Sections 2 and 3.1–3.3 explain attributor contextualism, the closure-related skeptical puzzle, and the proposed shift in knowledge-attribution standards as skeptical doubts become salient. Contextualism is disputed, not a consensus or proof that the skeptical scenario is actually or epistemically possible.
